However, no operator website, business registration, or independent record for a company operating under the name Strategic Datasphere could be located, and the absence of any discoverable web presence for a company using this specific name is itself worth weighing rather than assuming the name simply reflects an obscure but real business. reading.body:
Strategic Datasphere is an unconfirmed listing at a real Alpharetta office address, not a verified data center, and should not be counted in AI infrastructure analysis.

The entry carries no operator, no working website, no published specifications, and no independent record of a business under that name. The domain does not resolve. The address itself is real, a two story building on Union Hill Road in a north Atlanta technology corridor where genuine data center and network operators do exist, which is what makes the listing plausible enough to keep rather than delete.

Georgia has four data centers with published power specifications totaling 66.3 megawatts. This facility publishes no power figure, so it cannot be ranked among them. Thirty-three facilities are mapped in the state through OpenStreetMap, and most of those publish no capacity data either. The gap between what is mapped and what is measured is the normal condition of this dataset, not an anomaly of this one entry.

For AI specifically, the binding constraint is power and the buildings that deliver it. A facility with no megawatt figure and no confirmed operator tells you nothing about either. It cannot be placed on a load curve, counted toward a state total, or used to argue anything about grid pressure. The honest position is that it stays tagged as unconfirmed until evidence of current operation appears.
